assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry that made siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines clinically usable. This is a clear molecular-design principle (pKa-tuned lipids that are neutral in circulation and cationic in the endosome, formed by controlled mixing) that changed what clinicians can actually do, with enormous societal impact.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden, with MacLachlan in the siRNA-LNP work) built the core ionizable-lipid and rapid-mixing formulation concepts; Anderson and Langer at MIT made major lipid-library contributions and could be argued for as well. Credit is spread across academic and company teams, so a three-person split is contestable. I favour the Vancouver core.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale (patisiran 2018, COVID-19 mRNA vaccines 2020-21), with independent confirmation across many labs. Recognition is timely; the 2023 Medicine prize covered nucleoside modification but not the delivery vehicle.
uncertainties: Exact apportionment between the Vancouver group and the MIT group is disputed and I cannot verify patent and priority details from memory.
Some may view this as pharmaceutical formulation rather than core chemistry; I think the lipid design principles make it chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation through PROTACs and molecular glues is a new chemical modality that reprograms the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove proteins previously considered undruggable. It is conceptually original, rich in molecular design, and has opened a broad drug-discovery field with compounds in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001 PNAS); Handa's group identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later advances (VHL ligands, structural rationale, degrader design). The credited list has eight names, so choosing three is a hard cut.
assessment.maturity: Maturity is moderate: strong mechanistic and structural confirmation and a decade of work by many labs, but clinical proof is still emerging (ARV-471, ARV-110 phase 2/3 data; lenalidomide already approved as a molecular glue). Slightly early but approaching timely.
uncertainties: Late-stage clinical efficacy of PROTACs is not fully established.
Allocation between the PROTAC concept and the thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue discovery may need different laureates.
Sakamoto, Kim, Ciulli, Gray, Ito also have strong claims; I cannot resolve this from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, in which chemistry (reversible terminators, sequencing by synthesis, emulsion and bridge amplification, pyrosequencing on beads) reads billions of bases, transformed biology and medicine and made genomic diagnostics routine. The impact on what researchers and clinicians can do is hard to overstate.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry with single-molecule roots; Rothberg led the 454 and Ion Torrent platforms; Mayer and Ju also contributed (Lynx, Columbia terminators). Because several independent chemistries contributed, a clean three-person allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Technology is thoroughly mature and independently confirmed, with decades of impact; recognition is arguably overdue, although Sanger and Gilbert (1980) already cover the earlier generation of sequencing.
uncertainties: Competing claims among Solexa, 454, Lynx and Columbia teams.
Whether the prize committee views this as chemistry rather than medicine or technology is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing converts single-molecule interactions into electrical signals, enabling direct, label-free reading of DNA and RNA and a general single-molecule analytical platform. Protein engineering of the pore (alpha-hemolysin, MspA) and enzyme-controlled translocation are elegant molecular design, and portable sequencers now serve fieldwork and clinical settings.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer showed polynucleotide translocation in 1996; Bayley engineered pores and single-molecule stochastic sensing; Akeson demonstrated enzyme-ratcheted base-by-base reading. I propose Bayley, Akeson and Deamer. I believe Daniel Branton may be deceased (uncertain), which would affect eligibility.
assessment.maturity: Commercially validated and widely used, with independent confirmation across many labs. Timely, with a strong link between bioanalytical chemistry and medicine.
uncertainties: Branton's status and eligibility is something I cannot verify.
Credit may need to distinguish early concept (Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz) from engineering and sequencing realization (Bayley, Akeson).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allows site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids in living cells and organisms. This is a general molecular-design tool for protein engineering, biomaterials, bioorthogonal labeling and therapeutics, and I see its use widely in my own area.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the in vivo method and the first orthogonal pair for new amino acids; Wang was a key early contributor in Schultz's lab; Chin extended it with evolved ribosomes, quadruplet codons and whole-genome recoding. Yokoyama and Mehl also have claims (pyrrolysine system, platform generalization).
assessment.maturity: Mature and replicated in many labs for more than two decades; recognition would be timely. Not yet a mass-market technology, but a standard tool in chemical biology.
uncertainties: Allocation among Schultz, Chin, Wang and Yokoyama is uncertain.
Clinical translation is still limited compared with the technical reach.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics (shotgun/multidimensional protein identification, quantitative labeling and targeted approaches, high-resolution instrumentation) enables system-wide measurement of proteins and modifications and underpins biomarker discovery and clinical research. A major bioanalytical advance.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the usual core trio for large-scale proteomics; Hunt, Heck and Gygi contributed essential peptide sequencing, native and quantitative methods. The 2002 prize recognized ionization for macromolecules, so the instrumentation precedent is already set, which complicates novelty framing.
assessment.maturity: Mature and broadly validated. Recognition is timely to overdue, though overlap with the 2002 prize and with the Orbitrap and native MS candidates may fragment the field.
uncertainties: Overlap with other MS candidates (B004, B016) and the 2002 prize.
Selecting three of six credited names is an imperfect compromise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair into another without double-strand breaks by fusing deaminase chemistry to a programmable Cas protein. This is a clear chemical design principle with direct therapeutic reach, with patients already treated in trials and approvals approaching for genetic disease.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory invented cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead student and postdoc authors. Because Liu was the decisive and conceptual contributor, I propose him alone; a prize shared with other candidates in genome editing is also conceivable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and quickly, with clinical studies underway; the CRISPR-Cas9 chemistry prize of 2020 sets context. Slightly premature as the full therapeutic record is still being written, but strongly on track.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes and long-term safety remain unfolding.
Possible overlap with prime editing (B009), which would need a decision about joint or separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids established DNA as a programmable ligand for gold nanoparticles, with sharp melting transitions, colorimetric detection and intracellular gene regulation. This links nanomaterials, biosensing and medicine, close to my own field, and the molecular design principle is clear.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group published the 1996 DNA-nanoparticle assembly with Mucic and Storhoff; Alivisatos independently reported DNA-nanocrystal organization at the same time. Mirkin led the subsequent spherical nucleic acid development, so he is the key figure, with Alivisatos a possible co-recipient.
assessment.maturity: Real-world translation exists (Verigene diagnostics, SNA therapeutics in trials), though therapeutic benefit is not yet established. Moderately mature; recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical impact of spherical nucleic acids is still limited.
Priority between Mirkin and Alivisatos for the initial DNA-nanocrystal assembly is a point of attribution uncertainty.
